acceptance: A test asserts the emission of each of the two halt codes through the code path that emits it.
cmd/evolve is in go/.apicover-enforce, or the item records why it cannot be yet.
fix: Add a test that names both codes through the behaviour that emits them (the loop halt and the zero-ship halt), or unexport them if nothing outside the package reads them. Then check whether cmd/evolve has any other uncovered export; if it is clean, enrol it in go/.apicover-enforce so the gap cannot reopen.
source: console 2026-11-23: seen by four separate builders (#1702, #1627 rebuild, #1699 rebuild, #1624 rebuild) whose scoped apicover runs included cmd/evolve
summary: go/cmd/evolve/signal_loop.go exports CodeLoopHalt and CodeLoopZeroShipHalt, and no test names either. cmd/evolve is not in go/.apicover-enforce, so CI does not enforce it, but each builder that adds cmd/evolve to APICOVER_PKGS sees exit 2 and must work out that the gap is old. That cost time in four builds on 2026-11-23.
title: Name CodeLoopHalt and CodeLoopZeroShipHalt in a test, and enrol cmd/evolve in the API-coverage gate when it is clean
